t: Show HN: FELF – AppImage-like single binaries without FUSE, root, or a runtime
x: FELF — Fat ELF One executable file. Its own glibc. Runs on any Linux of the same architecture: no FUSE, no root, no runtime to install, nothing extracted to disk. Why You built a program. You want to hand it to someone and have it just work . On Linux, that's surprisingly hard: Copy the binary , and you get version 'GLIBC_2.38' not found or a missing libfoo.so.3 . A dynamic binary only runs where its exact libraries are. Link it statically , and glibc fights you: NSS, locales, iconv and dlopen want shared libraries. Hello HN!

I've always had a bad time redistributing programs that use shared libraries, AppImage in my opinion does too much, and a container is an overkill - not always integrates smoothly.

I've moved to nix since long ago, but redistributing between nix and other distros or vice versa it's still a pain in the ass, more so if you want to run an alien app in nix or a nix app without the package manger in any other distro.
